outcome: No concrete application bug identified; hosted timeout not reproduced locally. Test coordination has an avoidable zero-delay polling dependency.
root_cause_status: Coordination flakiness is a supported source-level explanation, not a proven reproduction of the hosted incident.

incident.failure: Five-second fail_after expired in final anyio.sleep(0) polling loop after native cancellation; prior source frozen app/test hashes unchanged from C21 acceptance

source_observations: Native task.cancel ends the route awaiter before the synchronous worker necessarily finishes. AnyIO cancellation is shielded until worker completion, so its branch waits differently.
Policy closed is set before actual CatalogueService.overview and JSON encoding. Final polling must therefore compete with all remaining worker computation and I/O.
Neither read-only actual route nor worker path contains an asynchronous cancellation checkpoint inside catalogue computation, and sanitized ordinary errors still build JSONResponse in that worker.
Zero-delay sleep keeps the event loop runnable; it is not an explicit cross-thread completion handshake.

Existing response stage is appended before JSONResponse.__init__, so original final condition proves encoding began on the worker, not that it completed. Proposed event is set after the actual constructor finishes.

scoped_experiment.qualification: Actual same route and configured sealed synthetic services. Candidate compiled only in memory. Enlarged switch interval deliberately stresses coordination; macOS local run does not establish exact Ubuntu CI scheduling cause.

changes: Use bounded threading.Event.wait through anyio.to_thread.run_sync for policy entry
Set an encoded Event after actual JSONResponse construction and wait on it with unchanged five-second timeout
Preserve all cancellation/no-delivery/thread-affinity assertions and assert closed after final encoded completion
